objective: Construct an infinite quadratic-deficit split family with exact cp certified by a modular K4 packing and signed weights; test asymptotic sufficiency of maximum-core one-stage potentials.

atomic_claims.text: For prime p>=3, b=p-1, a>=2p, t>=a, cp(K_a joined to (K_b disjoint union I_t))=at+ab-binom(a,2)-2binom(b,2).
The K4s indexed by unordered nonzero residue pairs and using their sum and product are edge-disjoint; a matching construction partitions all remaining edges.
For a=3b,t=4b, the three precisely restricted maximum-core strategies in Section 4 have minimum cost at least (11/64)n^2-O(n), while actual cp=(19b^2+5b)/2.
Nonmaximum core selection, two-stage residual recycling, and modular K4 packing give the three distinct upper constructions in Section 5.
If G=K_s joined to a clique-union residual on t>=s>=2 vertices, then cp(G)<=st-binom(s,2)+p<=n^2/6+2n, with p the number of nontrivial residual components.

assumptions: Finite simple graphs; exact edge partitions.
C01's written complete-graph matching decomposition and complete-split calculation are reused.
The modular construction uses arithmetic modulo a prime and proves its injectivity directly.
risks: Written primal and signed dual certificates only; no mathematical execution or verifier receipt.
The exact formula requires all displayed parameter restrictions.
The graphs are split and hence cannot negate the admitted existential domination target.
The failed-method statement concerns precisely the three restricted strategies, not every core-based or multi-stage method.
The universal-core theorem applies only to its stated subclass; the root remains open.

failed_route_proposal.blocker: Minimizing intact maximum clique, maximum-core mixed triangles plus singleton residue, and vertex-disjoint cliques plus singleton residue always yields n^2/6+O(n) for chordal graphs. This is an auxiliary-method proposal only: retain the admitted split-extremal route and root as open.
